reviewer: security-auditor / FABER fresh-context satellite; final frozen-source delta
qualification: Local-only first-party control boundary source review; no production, remote-admission or external-provider certification.

evidence.result: Foundation routes and OpenAPI are registered after the versioned owner middleware. Only health, owner session status and the separately HMAC-protected local command are exempted. Each protected request obtains its actor from identity.actor(headers) inside identity.exclusive; request JSON and legacy headers do not create actors.

Routes parse UUIDs and strict DTOs then pass the server actor to the broker. Environment/project and typed resource-reference checks remain in the broker. The owner intentionally has the global owner view; no project-service HTTP identity was added.

The HTTP/client allowlists expose resource/budget/plan preparation, exact approval, enqueue, owner cancellation/reconciliation and audit reads. They expose no worker claim, heartbeat, finish, grant authorization or epoch-advance endpoint. Returned run IDs, fence/epoch/lease metadata and grant IDs are owner metadata and do not supply a callable executor authority boundary.

Runtime constructs FoundationEngine without adapters. The adapter registry defaults empty and adapterFor requires an explicitly registered qualified adapter. New HTTP transport does not qualify providers or dispatch arbitrary commands.

Successful first-party JSON is parsed against its exact endpoint response schema before transmission. Invalid producer output becomes a safe generic 500; logs contain event/request ID/status/code only. Client requests, idempotency keys, version headers, bounded response bytes and success/error DTOs are checked before exposing values. Error JSON is not treated as a successful DTO.

OpenAPI is deterministic contract metadata behind the owner gate. The local-command schema documents its distinct HMAC authority and never embeds proof values. BetterAuth vendor WebAuthn remains a separately pinned /api/auth protocol with its existing endpoint allowlist; the native GitHub webhook keeps raw-byte signature authentication.

First-party DTO objects reject unknown fields, IDs are validated before client path construction, audit query keys reject duplicates/unknowns, and cursor/limit values are bounded. No free-form shell, SQL, filesystem path or credential sink was introduced by these transport changes.
